'''Murkowski''': {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}}
'''Ulmer''': {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Frank Murkowski]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Alaska sidebar}} The '''2002 Alaska gubernatorial election''' took place on November 5, 2002, for the post of [[List of governors of Alaska|Governor of Alaska]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Frank Murkowski]] defeated [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[List of Lieutenant Governors of Alaska|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Fran Ulmer]]. Murkowski became the first Republican elected governor of Alaska since [[Jay Hammond]] in [[1978 Alaska gubernatorial election|1978]]. ==Primaries== [[Incumbent]] Democratic Governor [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]] was [[term limit]]ed from running again. Lieutenant Governor Fran Ulmer easily won the Democratic [[Partisan primary|primary]] on August 27 against outsiders Michael Beasley and Bruce Lemke, neither of whom did much campaigning. Meanwhile, Senator Frank Murkowski also gained an easy win in the Republican primary.{{cite news| url = https://www.usatoday.com/news/politicselections/2002-08-27-primaries_x.htm.stm | archive-url = https://archive.today/20130205060630/http://www.usatoday.com/news/politicselections/2002-08-27-primaries_x.htm.stm | url-status = dead | archive-date = 2013-02-05 | title = Largent wins GOP nod for Oklahoma governor | access-date = 2008-07-19 | date = 2002-08-27| work=[[USA Today]]}}{{cite web| url = http://www.seattlepi.com/local/79778_alaska24.shtml | title = Alaska candidate wants to pack her heat | access-date = 2008-07-20 | date = 2002-07-24| website = seattlepi.com}}{{cite web|url=http://alaskalegislature.com/stories/081202/demgovernor.shtml |title=Democrats for governor: Ulmer, Lemke and Beasley |access-date=2008-07-20 |date=2002-08-12 |publisher=AlaskaLegislature.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060408000526/http://www.alaskalegislature.com/stories/081202/demgovernor.shtml |archive-date=2006-04-08 }} ==Campaign== Murkowski started the campaign as the clear favorite as Ulmer, despite being lieutenant governor, had a lot less [[name recognition]].{{cite news|url=http://archives.cnn.com/2002/ALLPOLITICS/10/22/elec02.ak.g/ |title=Alaska governor's race surprisingly close |access-date=2008-07-19 |date=2002-10-22 |publisher=[[CNN]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513231352/http://archives.cnn.com/2002/ALLPOLITICS/10/22/elec02.ak.g/ |archive-date=2008-05-13 |url-status=live }} Polls initially showed Ulmer about 20 percent behind Murkowski but as the campaign continued Ulmer closed on Murkowski in the polls by concentrating on local issues such as the state budget and by portraying herself as a moderate.{{cite web | url = http://www.peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102102/ele_102102ele0020001.shtml | title = Ulmer chases odds to be first woman governor | access-date = 2008-07-20 | date = 2002-10-21 | publisher = Kenai Peninsula Online | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110715064140/http://peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102102/ele_102102ele0020001.shtml | archive-date = 2011-07-15 | url-status = dead }} By October polls showed the candidates about level with one poll on October 17 showing Ulmer at 46% and Murkowski at 43%.{{cite web | url = http://www.peninsulaclarion.com/stories/101702/ala_101702ala0080001.shtml | title = Poll shows Ulmer closed gap with Murkowski | access-date = 2008-07-20 | date = 2002-10-17 | publisher = Kenai Peninsula Online | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110715064300/http://peninsulaclarion.com/stories/101702/ala_101702ala0080001.shtml | archive-date = 2011-07-15 | url-status = dead }} The biggest issue in the campaign was the economy and what to do about the projected budget shortfall in [[Alaska]]. The issue dominated the October [[debate]]s between the two candidates in [[Fairbanks, Alaska|Fairbanks]] and [[Anchorage, Alaska|Anchorage]].{{cite web | url = http://www.peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102302/ala_102302ala0110001.shtml | title = Murkowski and Ulmer face off in two debates in Fairbanks | access-date = 2008-07-19 | date = 2002-10-23 | publisher = Kenai Peninsula Online | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110715064028/http://peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102302/ala_102302ala0110001.shtml | archive-date = 2011-07-15 | url-status = dead }} Ulmer argued that the state should consider introducing a statewide tax for the first time since 1980 if the budget reserve fell too far and that state spending should be capped. However Murkowski opposed any new taxes and called his opponent pro-tax. He said that new oil prospects, high oil prices and revenues from other resources could close the gap in the budget.{{cite web | url = http://www.peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102402/ala_102402ala0140001.shtml | title = Fiscal gap dominates Anchorage debate | access-date = 2008-07-19 | date = 2002-10-24 | publisher = Kenai Peninsula Online | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110715064104/http://peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102402/ala_102402ala0140001.shtml | archive-date = 2011-07-15 | url-status = dead }} President [[George W. Bush]] made an advertisement supporting Murkowski, who also received support from Republicans [[Gale Norton]], [[Ted Stevens]] and [[Don Young]].{{cite news| url = https://www.usatoday.com/news/politicselections/2002-11-06-murkowski_x.htm | title = Career politician to head home state | access-date = 2008-07-20 | date = 2002-11-07| work=[[USA Today]] | first1=Jill | last1=Lawrence}} Ulmer received support from former Republican Governor [[Jay Hammond]], Governor [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]] and called on voters to support her so that Murkowski could stay working as Senator for Alaska in [[United States Congress|Congress]].{{cite web|url=http://www.businessweek.com/bwdaily/dnflash/nov2002/nf2002111_6042.htm |title=Post Time in the Gubernatorial Stakes |access-date=2008-07-20 |date=2002-11-01 |work=[[BusinessWeek]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050921003656/http://www.businessweek.com/bwdaily/dnflash/nov2002/nf2002111_6042.htm |archive-date=2005-09-21 }} During the campaign Murkowski refused to say whom he would appoint to serve his remaining two years as U.S. senator but after the election appointed his daughter [[Lisa Murkowski]], majority leader-elect in the [[Alaska House of Representatives]], to fill the seat.{{cite web | url = http://www.peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102202/ala_102202ala0030001.shtml | title = Stevens stumps for Murkowski in Fairbanks | access-date = 2008-07-20 | date = 2002-10-22 | publisher = Kenai Peninsula Online | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110715064332/http://peninsulaclarion.com/stories/102202/ala_102202ala0030001.shtml | archive-date = 2011-07-15 | url-status = dead }}{{cite web | url = http://www.peninsulaclarion.com/stories/122002/ala_122002alapm0010001.shtml | title = Gov. Murkowski appoints daughter to fill Senate seat | access-date = 2008-07-20 | date = 2002-12-20 | publisher = Kenai Peninsula Online | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081119131342/http://peninsulaclarion.com/stories/122002/ala_122002alapm0010001.shtml | archive-date = 2008-11-19 | url-status = dead }} ===Debate=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" |+ 2002 Alaska gubernatorial election debate |- ! scope="col" | {{abbr|No.|Number}} ! scope="col" | Date ! scope="col" | Host ! scope="col" | Moderator ! scope="col" | Link ! scope="col"| [[Republican Party (US)|Republican]] ! scope="col"| [[Democratic Party (US)|Democratic]] |- ! colspan="5" rowspan="2" |Key:
